title: upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 + fused rope + KV batching
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: reduce per-token latency and peak GPU memory for long-context autoregressive workloads by adopting FlashAttentionV2 kernels and fusing rotary/rope position ops with attention compute, while enabling KV-cache friendly batching paths. This PR upgrades the runtime attention implementation to a FlashAttentionV2-based codepath, introduces a fused QKV+rope kernel for common rotary/rope variants, and adds a KV-batching scheduling mode that coalesces simultaneous KV-cache lookups to avoid redundant memory traffic. Changes include kernel selection logic, fallback compatibility, unit/regression tests, microbenchmarks, and rollout gating. The goal is measurable latency and throughput improvements with no model-config breaking changes and a safe canary rollout for Dedicated and Hosted runtimes.
commits: introduce flashattnv2 kernel wrapper and build integration
implement fused qkv + rotary op and unit tests
add KV-batching scheduler and coalescing path for cache hits
kernel selection heuristics: sequence-length and model-profile driven
add microbench harness and perf tests, update CI matrix
docs: runtime config flags and rollout playbook
ci_checks: perf-microbench: pass (baseline vs flashattnv2 runs recorded)
review_comments: Liam: Can you summarize numerical stability tests for rotary variants? We've seen head-norm regressions previously.

Priya: Added deterministic fp32/fp16 unit tests reproducing forward/backward for rotary offsets and compared outputs with reference implementation; differences <1e-5 for fp32, <1e-3 for fp16. Included in runtime/tests/attention_perf_test.cc.
Ravi: KV-batching looks promising; how does this interact with existing per-client isolation in Dedicated?

Priya: KV-batching only coalesces reads within a single worker process and respects tenant isolation; added config flag runtime.scheduling.kv_coalesce.enable (default true for mainline) and dedicated rollout notes in docs.
release_notes: Upgrade attention runtime: FlashAttentionV2 kernels, fused QKV+rotary ops, and KV-cache coalescing scheduler. Expect ~15-25% p50 latency improvement on long-context generation and up to 20-30% throughput gain for batchy workloads. Opt-in flags and canary rollout plans provided.
benchmark_summary: GPT-like 8k context p50 latency: -18% on g4dn.12xlarge (fp16, batch=1, autoreg)
GPT-like 32k context throughput: +24% on 8xA100 (fp16, batch packing enabled)
Memory peak: -12% on large sequence lengths due to fused rope and reduced intermediate copies
rollout_plan: Canary on Dedicated pool (5% traffic) -> monitor p50/p99 latency and token-cost regression alerts for 48h -> expand to 25% -> full rollout. Hosted API gated by feature flag and gradual region-by-region enablement.
notes: This PR includes non-breaking runtime flags and model-profile driven heuristics to maintain backward compatibility. We kept the original attention codepath as fallback and included explicit fallbacks for unsupported hardware (older CUDA or compute capability).
